newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Global Coalition for Africa to tackle corruption.
newsitem.headline: Global Coalition for Africa to tackle corruption.

text.p: Corruption in Africa will top the agenda at a high-level meeting of the Global Coalition for Africa in Maputo, Mozambique in November, coalition officials said on Saturday.

"Corruption is an important impediment to confidence-building..., to investment and to trade," Dutch Development Minister Jan Pronk said in Ivory Coast after a two-day meeting of the Coalition, centred on trade issues.
The Global Coalition for Africa describes itself as a North-South forum seeking to build consensus between African governments, Western donors, aid groups and companies active in Africa.
Pronk stressed that corruption was not simply an African fault. "Very often the corruptor lives abroad...Corruption is still in many countries tax-deductible," he said.

One proposal the Coalition may pursue is for firms wanting to bid for foreign projects to state publicly that corrupt practices would not be tolerated. Culprits would be punished and firms that transgressed excluded from tenders.

Coalition officials welcomed a recent U.S. government initiative to promote trade with Africa, which they said could mean as much as $500 million being pumped into infrastructure on the continent, and $150 million invested in telecommunications.
But Kwesi Botchwey, president of the Coalition's economic committee, was concerned that the initiative might be seized on by people seeking to put an end to development aid.
"It's a move in the right direction but it shouldn't be seen as a way of cutting off all assistance," he said.
